title: Aurora: Prefetch Tuning and Rollout Handbook
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Objective: Produce an operational handbook that sequences experiments, rollout criteria, and runbooks for adaptive prefetching and quantization profiles across hosted and dedicated deployments.

Scope:
- Define measurable goals (tokens saved, p95 latency, regression thresholds) for prefetch TTLs and adaptive batching heuristics.
- Create a decision log for choosing TTL-based vs. demand-driven prefetch and for selecting per-model quant profiles.
- Deliver automation for canary rollouts, automatic rollback triggers, and dashboards that surface signal quality regressions (per-prompt eval set).
- Hand off runbooks and a minimal SDK extension that exposes tuning knobs to infra and SRE teams.

Why now: We have several ad-hoc prefetch pilots with inconsistent rollback criteria and no unified acceptance criteria for quantization. This initiative standardizes the rollout path so savings are reproducible and low-risk for customer-facing traffic.
acceptance_criteria: Playbook doc with step-by-step rollout checklist (smoke checks, canary baseline, traffic ramp percentages)
Three validated prefetch policies (TTL-static, TTL-adaptive, demand-cache) with measured token-savings and p95 latency impact on selected workloads
Quant profile matrix for top 5 serving models with automated regression tests and <1% user-visible quality drop on eval sets
Canary automation: gating rules in CI that abort rollout on quality signal or latency slippage
Runbooks published in Confluence and linked from Console; handoff session scheduled with SRE and Solutions Eng

notes:
Tradeoffs: TTL-adaptive gives quick wins on short-chat flows but can increase tail latency on long-sequence workloads; plan includes kernel-level caps and a per-route whitelist to exclude high-latency-sensitive customers.
